ruling.recommended_action: Send to human safety review: obtain both parties' statements and any in-app incident report; assess the rider's threat against the driver under Ryde's code of conduct (SAFE-1) and record the outcome on the rider's account. No fare or fee adjustment is made by this ruling.
ruling.reasoning: This is a driver-filed safety dispute. The chat is short and fully timestamped: the driver asked the rider not to smoke in the car at 18:24 [F3], and the rider replied at 18:24 "Say that again and I will punch you." [F4], on a record where every message carries a timestamp [F5]. A punch threat aimed at the other party is not a route argument or mere rudeness; it is a threat of physical violence directed at the driver, and Ryde's code of conduct bars "Assault, harassment, or abuse of any kind ... including Threats and Intimidation" [SAFE-1]. The driver's post-trip statement corroborates the same account and adds that he kept driving and did not answer [F6]. Where a threat appears in the chat or a complaint, no automatic ruling is issued and the case goes to a person with a factual summary [SAFE-1]; the trace confirms this branch is the only allowed outcome.
ruling.escalation_reason: Confirmed threat of violence in the chat: rider replied "Say that again and I will punch you." to the driver's no-smoking request [F3][F4][F6]. Under SAFE-1 the case takes no automatic ruling and goes to human safety review. Route and fare are not in dispute and need no adjustment: actual distance equals the optimal route (+0.0 km) and duration was 3.1 min shorter than estimate, on a metered RydeTAXI fare of $20.75 [F1][F2]. Nothing in the record shows any prior safety or dispute history for either party [F7][F8]; the reviewer should check the rider's account for prior conduct incidents.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider advocate's requested outcome of no_action cannot stand on this record: the rider's own chat message threatens to punch the driver [F4], which is a threat of violence under SAFE-1, and a safety case takes no automatic ruling.

The driver advocate's requested outcome of no_action likewise cannot be granted as a closed ruling, even though the driver's account is credible [F6]: under SAFE-1 a confirmed threat requires escalation to a human reviewer rather than a final ruling either way.
